findings.title: Exhausted federated recovery-codes credential is removed via local store only
findings.body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(authenticatedUser)` now prefers the credential returned by the user storage provider (`getFederatedCredentialsStream`). When that federated model reports `allCodesUsed()`, the code still calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`, which only touches Keycloak's local credential table. For a credential that lives in user storage this is a no-op (the exhausted codes remain in the external store and `isConfiguredFor` keeps returning true), and if the provider did not assign an id to the model (`RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues` does not set one) the JPA store is asked to find an entity with a null id, which throws `IllegalArgumentException` and turns the last successful recovery-code login into a 500. The federated branch needs to go through the storage provider (e.g. `disableCredentialType`) instead of `removeStoredCredentialById`, or skip removal when the credential did not come from local storage.

findings.title: Login form bean still unconditionally unwraps Optional; federated providers without getCredentials() crash the page
findings.body: The bean now looks up the credential via `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` but still calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` without checking presence. With this PR, `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.configuredFor` returns true as soon as the user storage provider's `isConfiguredFor(..., recovery-authn-codes)` returns true, so the recovery-code form is rendered for federated users. However `CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials()` has a default implementation returning an empty stream; a provider that implements `supportsCredentialType`/`isConfiguredFor`/`isValid`/`updateCredential` for recovery codes (everything the feature otherwise requires) but does not override `getCredentials()` makes `getCredential()` return `Optional.empty()`, and the login page fails with `NoSuchElementException` (HTTP 500) for every such user. Either handle the empty case (e.g. fall back to a generic prompt without a code number) or clearly document in `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential`/release notes that providers must implement `getCredentials()` returning a `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel`.

findings.title: getCredentials() dereferences getMyUser() without null check
findings.body: `getCredentials(realm, user)` does `var myUser = getMyUser(user);` and immediately accesses `myUser.recoveryCodes` and `myUser.otp`. Every other method in this provider (`isConfiguredFor`, `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`, `isValid`) guards against `getMyUser` returning null, which happens for users not present in the in-memory map (e.g. a user adapter still referenced after `removeUser`, or a user from a different component instance sharing the realm). Since `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` is now invoked from the browser authenticator and the login form bean on every recovery-code login, this becomes an NPE surfacing as a 500 instead of an empty stream. Return `Stream.empty()` when `myUser == null`.

findings.title: Provider claims recovery-codes support but cannot disable or report them as disableable
findings.body: `supportsCredentialType` and `isConfiguredFor` were extended to return true for `recovery-authn-codes`, and `updateCredential` stores them, but `disableCredentialType` still only handles OTP (recovery codes fall into the 'Unsupported to disable' branch) and `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` never reports the type. As a result the admin REST `disableCredentialType` and the account-console credential removal for a federated user holding recovery codes silently do nothing, and the new test only exercises setup + login. The disable/remove path for federated recovery codes (the analogue of `testDisableCredentialsInUserStorage` / `testOTPSetupAndRemoveThroughAccountMgmtAndLogin`) is therefore untested.

findings.title: Federated recovery-code test does not cover invalid code, code consumption, or exhaustion
findings.body: `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` only verifies a single successful login with code #0. The test storage's `isValid` never marks a code as used and `getCredentials()` rebuilds a fresh `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` on each call, so `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode()` is always 0 and `allCodesUsed()` is never true. Consequently the new federated-storage branches in `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` (credential removal / re-adding `CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES` when codes are exhausted) and the rejection of a wrong code for a federated user are not exercised at all. Add at least a negative login attempt and a scenario where the provider reports all codes used.
